t: Particle Collider: Magnet Field Math — Simple
name: Particle Collider: Magnet Field Math — Simple
title: Particle Collider: Magnet Field Math — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] Dipoles bend the beam: Bρ = p/q, so a 7 TeV proton in the LHC's 27 km ring needs 8.3 T dipoles. The desk computes the field per ring — the magnet is sized by the momentum.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: Dipole field for 7 TeV protons, 4.3 km bend radius = 5.4 T. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.
real_world_basis: Magnetic rigidity math is the real basis of synchrotron design.
signature_version: Signature version: the collider magnet desk — the chapter's machine as the field target, with the speculative framing labeled concept.
build_steps: Build: the field quality matters as much as the strength — specify both.
math_note: Dipole field for 7 TeV protons, 4.3 km bend radius: 5.4 T [verified]; Zeeman splitting at 8.3 T (electron): 961 µeV [verified]

math_check.label: Dipole field for 7 TeV protons, 4.3 km bend radius
math_check.note: corrected 2026-10-19: was '8.3 T' (that is the LHC value at 2.8 km radius)

safety: Magnet safety: quench protection on every superconducting magnet — always.
how_it_works: Divide the beam rigidity by the bend radius for the field. The demo sizes three rings.
requirements: Re-run the demo program to re-verify every number
standards: Full-file record, never a stub
